keyFacts: What we learned from a year of four-day weeks
By Maya Ortiz · March 4, 2026 · 7 min read

Last March we tried something our board called “brave” and our accountant called “unwise”: every team would work Monday to Thursday, with Friday off and no cut in pay. We promised to measure everything and to stop if it didn’t work.

We expected output to fall. Instead, most teams shipped slightly more, and the number of late projects dropped by a third. The biggest change was not speed but focus: people stopped filling Fridays with meetings that could have been an email.
“I get more done in four focused days than I used to in five scattered ones.”
That line came from our support lead, and it summed up the survey.
Even the two teams whose numbers dipped asked to keep the schedule and fix the problems instead.

We’re keeping it. Next year we’ll publish the full data set, including the parts that didn’t go well.

keyFacts: The Quiet Return of the Night Train
By Hannah Okafor · November 9, 2026 · 8 min read

Ten years ago, the sleeper train looked finished. Budget airlines had taken the routes, the carriages were old, and operators were cutting services every winter. Today new lines open every season, and many of them sell out weeks in advance.
What changed was not the trains themselves but the travellers. Families, remote workers and people avoiding short flights now treat a night on the rails as part of the trip rather than a cost of it.
"You go to sleep in one country and wake up in another. No airport has ever given me that."
